body:
Democrats are flooding red states with outside money. Montana cannot be the one that slips away. |

FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR JOHN THUNE:
I want to be direct with you about something I am watching closely.

Democrats are not just playing defense this cycle. They are on offense - targeting red states they have no business competing in, flooding them with outside money, and running candidates specifically designed to fool voters into thinking they are getting a moderate when they are actually getting another loyal Schumer vote.

**Montana is one of those states. But I refuse to let it slip away without a fight.**

**[Fellow Conservative, that is why I am asking you to stand with Trump-endorsed Kurt Alme today.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=e59f3527c3fb4c4d8e725ccfef75f0ed&_e=hEPvqCpuowcq2dEim1qzNKwDLsaQzRnybKG1PafCp6ZVW3B52s8z4twbcsObMqzS7cBHr_AHfBFi168mR2obNOzG_8lgKOffOL7jQh3BUntWwlZ2k3HBPdPcwS6gjFATS2OxWAwa6tXW5NC10MQJyLI4vXwGbPTNq1tJJ7PrLLVmxmSoVE2I2Dqg9AwyqWlguaQGOTj16BA3SMo5UJhtv3a6Y-Mjk3oxWde9lOt5lMgNlmeEwlkbbSEXhBFCfVQGNhqF8M4anWClE7ONyf820suN2MQAqlZXqvdG7diDEp5fIMm9KjQ6TqHW-2NY9HiVvKPW7Y8mpOeFd8_QD4rYVry8E0b7nkOoQhdoitrP1ognX6ROOJXth3CgvcCWOeBz7fJj22gLIKj_JPQe6s6ZV-p7RzCCsdWGx1DB4wS04eC-Tw_-qLy0tgGC7CUbg8_GBShPBAVmMlSVuEPFkC4pAsIy9xy1plKtHi-2bv6HeK0XdRRtAvE9eBci6XUtV8pxxVmK1BF3eOoewyS3s2MB8fVXvMTuX9zxb9ixHHuy91wOE-gkc-WNX2aJ0AZB9s6WMPRI1k3tlbCG30vkWmXkQsFwITnGiC66yGBQzOvlB4feGscI7QeWT6_rAqqCzsgdbyNEPse3DKCrbMaWCoXBV7Bbe2_njW_l39uvT0VeVOHJGFFszusi-ZV9eMGf9jFufDPGywyztOyi8VVfnu8iTWGP3Ls2p1AXU4R4uE666ko%3D) ** [**STAND WITH KURT >>**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=e59f3527c3fb4c4d8e725ccfef75f0ed&_e=hEPvqCpuowcq2dEim1qzNKwDLsaQzRnybKG1PafCp6ZVW3B52s8z4twbcsObMqzS7cBHr_AHfBFi168mR2obNOzG_8lgKOffOL7jQh3BUntWwlZ2k3HBPdPcwS6gjFATS2OxWAwa6tXW5NC10MQJyLI4vXwGbPTNq1tJJ7PrLLVmxmSoVE2I2Dqg9AwyqWlguaQGOTj16BA3SMo5UJhtv3a6Y-Mjk3oxWde9lOt5lMgNlmeEwlkbbSEXhBFCfVQGJy1_oQ7lMgMjeqfybedLwJ-jrC7IyWKc6qd_ClIL1NHArbsJzON021HHO827MO6NEf7GwhLrK_aKCDPdE4FOaVxqUSIGbuqbxC2d-2D9t9N34xr8XrWyXhuxdKk7RjOjd_a0d2ybOPRy4Q6BdJwhNrE7QdwxiamtP1-Lzmwolz8P3fnUeY7f7QWTMkVnEGKkClvxFIrv8mxuGUQv3g2lS_PFjI82e7-BEG_wgUlNdt3sICFQ_oTiPkCYwdi-IQaXzVF6fHQ7_h7h0wj-b8vLg3dxJyPRQatK1WLJNQOzOKMcExH0T4GZ3t17W05644KDjGLxVOu7kgZmHg06ulaNPjKkroZ8i2ghZm1S8YIw8yBlhkjbI9y9ABrvYXndDSNkK3FrP7vIGDS95lYPmMubdTnStbCk2n9qLEgzSOEVuPkGSjaM_KjeLKtvAZf3mPkJigzfmVEtmGBg1N2he7Mlw1Qq2RrkPHqBrfHHAaf4nVc%3D)
I have served in the Senate long enough to know how these races unfold. Democrats identify a target, recruit a candidate, and pour in millions of dollars before the Republican side has had time to build. By the time conservatives see what is happening, the gap is already significant.

I refuse to let that happen here.

Kurt Alme is exactly the kind of candidate Montana needs - a Trump-nominated federal prosecutor with a real record of results. He took on cartels, drug traffickers, and violent criminals as U.S. attorney. He cut Montana's income tax rate. He helped make Montana debt-free. **_He has President Trump's complete and total endorsement, and mine._**

But here is the reality. Schumer has two candidates in this race, both funded by out-of-state money, both running the same bait-and-switch playbook we have seen in state after state. They are not running to represent Montana. They are running to give the Senate back to Chuck Schumer.

Fellow Conservative, maintaining our Senate Republican Majority is not just about this seat - it is about our ability to confirm conservative judges, advance President Trump's agenda, and provide a check on Washington's excesses. _Every seat matters. This one especially._

We are less than two weeks out from Election Day. Ballots are out, and Nevadans are already voting. I wanted to check in to walk through what's at stake on Election Day - and what you'll find on your ballot when you go to vote.
Nevadans have a lot of big choices this November, including major offices and critical ballot measures. Up and down the ballot, the choices you make will shape life in our state for years to come: what you pay for groceries and rent, whether your family has access to healthcare, and whether your freedoms are protected.
**We need Aaron Ford to be Nevada 's next governor.**
The governor's office is the single most powerful position in our state government. Nevada families need someone in that office who will stand up to Donald Trump and who wakes up every morning thinking about them. That's why I'm proud to endorse Aaron Ford for governor.
Aaron grew up working class, is a former public school math teacher, and served as State Senate Majority Leader in the Nevada Legislature. He knows how hard Nevada families are being squeezed right now. He's laser-focused on the issues that matter most, from tackling the affordable housing crisis to defending every student's right to a quality education.
As attorney general, Aaron has spent his time fighting for Nevadans, and he's exactly the governor our state needs. He knows our communities, he shows up, and he gets things done. And I know he'll keep fighting the good fight as our next governor.
**And we need a lieutenant governor, an attorney general, and a secretary of state who are ready to work with him.**
Downballot races don't always get the attention they deserve, but who we elect this year will matter enormously. We need to give Aaron a partner in the governor's office, and the best person for the job is Sandra Jauregui. Sandra has served our state well as a leader in the Nevada Assembly, and I know she'll keep working to expand affordable housing, lower healthcare costs, reduce gun violence, and create good-paying jobs as our next lieutenant governor.
We need Nicole Cannizzaro to take the reins as attorney general. Nevadans need an AG who will be a champion for consumers against powerful special interests, take on the Trump administration's abuses of power, and stand up for the rule of law. Nicole has the experience as a prosecutor and legislative leader to do this job and deliver for hardworking families.
And we need Cisco Aguilar to fend off his extreme MAGA opponent one more time and keep up his work protecting our elections and serving Nevada's small businesses. As secretary of state, Cisco has made sure every eligible Nevadan can cast a ballot and have it counted. At a time when democracy itself is under attack, Cisco's work has never been more important.
**We also have the opportunity to send four strong Democrats to Washington to keep fighting for Nevada families.**
Nevada has four congressional races on the ballot this year, and each one will make a difference on the balance of power in Washington. We need to re-elect Dina Titus, Susie Lee, and Steven Horsford to the House of Representatives. They fight for Nevada every single day, and I'm proud to work alongside them.
And we need to send Teresa Benitez-Thompson to Washington to join them. A former social worker and state legislator, Teresa is fired up and ready to bring her experience and her commitment to Nevada families to Congress. Polls show this race is highly competitive. By flipping this longtime Republican seat in Northern Nevada, we'll put Democrats in an incredible position to take back the House and put a real check on Donald Trump's dangerous, self-serving agenda.
**You 'll also see an important question on your ballot this year:**
* **Vote YES on Question 6** to permanently protect the right to abortion in Nevada. If "Question 6" rings a bell, it's because it was on the ballot in 2024, and it passed. But under Nevada law, ballot measures must pass twice to become law. **So let 's pass this for good this year and make sure reproductive freedom is always protected in Nevada.**

**Here 's what I'm asking you to do right now, before you move on from this Substack.**
It will only take a minute. Please, open your calendar - whether it's on your phone or hanging on the wall - and make your plan to vote. When and how will you cast your ballot? Will you mail it back? Drop it off? Vote in person during early voting? Do you need a ride or a plan to take public transit?
Pick your voting day, put it on your calendar, and tell a friend or family member so they can hold you accountable. Then ask them what their plan is, too.
Elections are won by the people who show up, and every conversation you have with a neighbor makes a difference. Between these races, we have a real shot at putting a Democrat in the governor's office and helping flip the House blue. That would change what's possible for Nevada families and for families across the country.
But we can't do it without you. Democratic candidates are facing well-funded opposition, and the final two weeks are when every dollar goes furthest: reaching voters, getting out the vote, and making sure no one sits this one out.
**We 're working to raise $50,000 by midnight, and it would mean a lot to have you with us.**
**[So I'm asking you directly: Will you pitch in $5 or anything you can spare to split between my campaign and Nevada Democrats before midnight?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/556dc4b0-dc30-4c34-879b-43abf9bf1338?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thank you for everything you do for Nevada. Let's finish this election season with wins worth celebrating!
Jacky

Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan of the United Arab Emirates at an event Villa on September 10, 2026 in Berlin, Germany. Photo by Omer Messinger/Getty Images.
A private intelligence firm working for the United Arab Emirates compiled a database of thousands of Facebook users living inside the country--using their social media activity, including likes of news outlets critical of the UAE--to identify what the firm described as "hostile" individuals during a broader crackdown on political expression in the country.
Information about the database comes from a leaked archive from Geneva-based Alp Services reviewed by Drop Site News. The social media mapping operation resulted in the creation of a series of spreadsheets with over 11,300 entries for Facebook users living in the UAE including their names, places of residence, employment, and other personal information.
The criteria for inclusion in the database--submitted to an Emirati client in January 2018--included liking Facebook pages published by news outlets and political groups deemed hostile to the UAE. Documents contained in the archive show that the firm received €55,000 for the work, carried out under the project code name "Arnica 2."
The UAE has continued to aggressively monitor social media for any signs of dissent, with hundreds of individuals [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/223c97ca-040a-408b-9929-9392c8627e74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this year over their online posts related to the Iran war.
The archive was obtained by Mediapart and provided to the reporting consortium European Investigative Collaborations. Drop Site previously [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/9716dc3b-ceb4-4d67-a6de-d7555c9dd0d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Alp Services' work for the UAE on a planned smear campaign targeting American Muslims. Other details from the archive were previously [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/aef82d83-e0a2-4836-b3b3-ea8fcf634228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the New Yorker.
Alp Services and the UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not respond to requests for comment.
The Facebook mapping project began during a particularly dangerous period for political expression inside the Emirates. In June 2017, amid an escalating confrontation with Qatar--which included a blockade against that country--the country's general prosecutor [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/6e9a7f63-7ce3-48b0-9bc0-54ad02e2b109?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that people expressing sympathy for Doha or objections to the government's measures against it could face up to 15 years in prison. Initial work on the Alp project began one month after this warning.
The Arnica 2 project was proposed to help identify alleged political threats inside the UAE. In addition to cataloging critics of the UAE's policy toward Qatar, the project also offered to help target alleged supporters of the Muslim Brotherhood--a fixation of the Emirati ruler Mohammed bin Zayed since the Arab Spring.
In a planning document produced by Alp, under the heading "Social media intelligence to identify hostile supporters in your jurisdiction," the firm laid out the assistance it could offer to Abu Dhabi in its crackdown.
"Through our team of in-house social media intelligence analysts, we could identify hundreds of individuals based in your country that publicly 'like' hostile groups, especially the MB," the firm wrote, offering to use its "proprietary tools and advanced mapping software," to find "interesting intelligence and new leads."
Alp identified approximately 1,000 Muslim Brotherhood "supporters" who lived in the UAE, claiming that many of them were employed at different levels of Emirati society or in its security services. "Amongst them, we notably find people who declare working for either the Dubai or the Abu Dhabi police, as well as numerous teachers, students and other employees," Alp wrote in a July 2017 report. The document, which included personal information about these individuals, some of whose names were duplicated in the archive, did not provide evidence substantiating their affiliation beyond likes for Facebook pages affiliated with the Brotherhood or Arabic-language news outlets critical of UAE policies.
Alp appeared to treat this research as preliminary work that could be used to showcase the services it could offer Abu Dhabi in digging deeper to find possible dissent. "While we already have some preliminary 'raw' findings, should the topic be of interest to you, we could launch a full-scale analysis," a representative of Alp wrote in an August 2017 message.
Thousands of ordinary individuals residing in the country are included in several spreadsheets compiled by Alp for its Emirati client. The lists include individuals identified by their employment as engineers, pharmacists, restaurant workers, and others whose only recorded connection to the investigation was membership in Facebook groups or liked pages.
"We cannot establish what happened to the 11,300 individuals without knowing whether the database was passed to Emirati State Security and subsequently used operationally. But given what we know about Abu Dhabi's security apparatus, I would be very concerned about the potential consequences", said Dr. Andreas Krieg, an academic focused on the Middle East at the School of Security Studies at King's College London.
Krieg added that the UAE has an extensive internal security apparatus based on digital surveillance, intelligence gathering and political profiling. "Its principal objective is not simply to identify criminal activity but to detect and pre-empt any form of political mobilisation outside state control," he said. "A database containing people's names, workplaces, residences and alleged political associations would be extremely valuable to that apparatus."
In addition to this mass sweep of alleged dissidents found on social media, some well-known individuals and organizations involved in political and human rights activism also seem to have been profiled. Among them was a profile belonging to Ahmed Mansoor, identifying his location as Dubai and past employment with the Gulf Center for Human Rights. Mansoor, a prominent Emirati human rights activist who served on the advisory board of the center, had already been arrested in March 2017, several months before the report was compiled. The following year he was sentenced to ten years in prison over Facebook and Twitter posts calling for political reform in the UAE.
## "Strictly Confidential"
An August 28, 2017 working document labeled "client request" listed ten Facebook pages for investigation, with its search links combining a filter for apparent UAE residents with one for people who liked each page. The pages included those for Arabic-language news outlets UAE71, Arabi21, Al Araby, Rassd, UAE Studies, Emirati Affairs, and Al Dabboor.
Three of those outlets--Arabi21, Rassd, and Al-Araby Al-Jadeed--had also appeared in the demands issued to Qatar that June by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, and Egypt amid the standoff between Doha and those countries over the Arab Spring. The bloc sought their closure, along with Al Jazeera and other outlets it accused Qatar of funding.
Alp outsourced part of the Facebook mapping project to a subcontractor firm called Total Trust Investigations, based in Bucharest, Romania, according to documents in the archive. On August 31, 2017, Alp employee Lionel Badal sent a contact there seven search links and asked for names and profile information to be provided in Excel format.
Total Trust Investigations did not respond to a request for comment.
"Some will be so long that we cannot scroll down to see how many people there are," he wrote. "Obviously, if your IT can develop a small software to do the job automatically, that would be even better," he added. "Of course, and as always, this request is strictly confidential."
Badal forwarded the correspondence to colleagues, including Alp chief Mario Brero, identifying the lists as Arnica 2 material.
In October 2017, Alp's Emirati contact, Matar Humaid al-Neyadi, who currently serves as the UAE's ambassador to Kuwait, requested and received a proposal from Alp that set out a 55,000 euro budget for analyzing 10 Facebook pages and their audiences. Internal records show Alp billed that amount to ARIAF Studies and Research LLC in Abu Dhabi in December, and delivered the data on a USB drive the following month.
## Chilled Speech
Alp's internal documents do not establish what consequences followed from the lists it provided the UAE. But the mapping project came at a time when UAE authorities were increasingly seeking to prosecute online political expression.
The crackdown had roots in the Arab Spring. In 2011, with demands spreading across the region for political change, a group of 133 Emirati citizens signed a petition asking for the establishment of an elected Federal National Council that would enjoy some legislative powers. The request was denied and the government began repressing political dissent of all types, accusing critics of association with the Muslim Brotherhood and even [expanding](https://substack.com/redirect/9716dc3b-ceb4-4d67-a6de-d7555c9dd0d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its efforts globally.
"The Brotherhood has become a catch-all category through which Abu Dhabi can delegitimize political opponents, independent Muslim organisations, journalists, academics and civil society actors. Some of these individuals have genuine connections to Islamist movements. Many do not," said Krieg. "The underlying logic is guilt by association, where extremely tenuous relationships are transformed into evidence of a supposedly coordinated transnational conspiracy."
In November 2012, the Emirati government passed a cybercrimes law that set out new offenses, effectively banning criticism of senior Emirati officials and advocacy of political reform. Human Rights Watch officials [described](https://substack.com/redirect/6609d2d9-35e9-407b-810d-f2be4f64f64e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the new law as an attempt to ban "even the most tempered criticism" of Abu Dhabi and its regional policies.
By the time Alp began compiling its Facebook lists, prison sentences for online expression had already become standard practice. In March 2017, a UAE court sentenced Jordanian journalist Tayseer al-Najjar to three years in prison and a large fine over Facebook posts criticizing Egypt, Israel, and Gulf countries. Later that month, academic Nasser bin Ghaith received a ten-year sentence on charges that included comments on Twitter about his treatment in an earlier prosecution. Amnesty International described bin Ghaith as a prisoner of conscience and [denounced](https://substack.com/redirect/8b703d74-43a8-4efd-affa-708d83d9d353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the allegations against him based on his social media posts as "ludicrous."
In July 2024, dozens of defendants in a new mass trial received life sentences for their involvement in a political advocacy group called the Justice and Dignity Committee, which the Emirati government had classified as a terrorist organization. The evidence, and even the allegations against the group--which has been described as an independent advocacy group with no involvement in political violence by Human Rights Watch--has been kept under strict control by the Emirati government. In March 2025, the UAE's Federal Supreme Court rejected appeals of the convictions.
The archive of Alp documents does not establish that the Arnica 2 project contributed to any of these prosecutions. But in its July 2017 report highlighting the tenuous online connections of teachers and police officers to human rights and civil society groups, the company promised to work harder to find evidence that could be used to determine that they were "hostile supporters" of causes at odds with the Emirati government.
"Of course, further enquiries would be required in order to confirm this initial intelligence," an Alp representative wrote, "but work is ongoing."

Halloween is right around the corner. **But few things are spookier than the thought of John Sununu heading back to the Senate.**
Election Day is just 12 days away, and Sununu and Republicans are counting on Granite Staters to look the other way. We can't let that happen.
Donald Trump hand-picked John Sununu to run here in New Hampshire, because Trump knows that Sununu is the GOP's best shot at flipping a Senate seat anywhere in the country. That's why Republicans and their allies are spending more than $60 million to buy this seat for him, betting that a famous political name and a lot of outside money will be enough.
This race is neck and neck, and I'm counting on this team to help us keep up. **[If you can chip in $5, $15, or whatever works for you to help us compete with the dark money pouring into New Hampshire.](https://substack.com/redirect/b74d3a9b-27a0-4321-91e1-85638c9183ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/b74d3a9b-27a0-4321-91e1-85638c9183ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Sununu 's record is the scariest thing on the ballot. **Here's a quick reminder of what's at stake:
**John Sununu said this race is "important to President Trump's agenda." **Trump and MAGA Republicans are backing Sununu, because they know he'll rubber-stamp their extreme agenda, even when it doesn't serve New Hampshire.
**He 'll sell out Granite Staters.** John Sununu voted to serve corporate special interests like Wall Street, Big Pharma, and Big Oil -- then cashed in with those same industries as his net worth surged by up to $35 million.
**He has deep pockets behind him.** More than $60 million is flowing in from Republicans and their allies, including Trump's No Going Back PAC, the Koch network, and Elon Musk. We need the resources to make sure Granite Staters hear the truth about his record.
The contrast is clear. But with 12 days left, we don't have much time to make our case to every voter.

clean_body: This isn’t politics as usual. And it shows you how desperate the GOP is to hold on to this governor’s seat. | Peter, Vivek Ramaswamy just crossed a line. We’re not going to link to his campaign’s new attack ad against Amy Acton and risk amplifying it any further. Suffice it to say that independent observers have called it “vile,” “revolting,” and “unbelievably disgusting.” After some fellow Republicans called him out, the Ramaswamy campaign doubled down — announcing it was spending $4 million to get it in front of Ohio voters. This is how desperate they are to hold on to the Ohio governorship, and recent polls have Ramaswamy falling behind. So they’re stooping to new lows in order to save their electoral behinds. The governor of Ohio is a top electoral priority for the NDRC, because he (or, soon, she) holds a seat on the state’s redistricting commission — and has veto power over any gerrymanders the heavily Republican state legislature tries to pass. For over a decade, Ohio has been run entirely by Republicans. And they’ve abused their power to pass some of the worst gerrymanders in the country — shamelessly ignoring court orders and voter-approved redistricting reforms to do so. Electing Amy Acton will end that era of one-party rule in Ohio. That’s what is at stake on November 3rd. body:
We don’t have to accept a system that prioritizes the 1% over the safety of working people.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261022-6869-footer&t=1&akid=6869%2E420207%2EYy7dor)
Let's take a look at some numbers, Peter:
* The top 1% in this country own more wealth than the bottom 93%
* _One single man_ — Elon Musk — owns more wealth than the bottom 53% of households
* In the last year alone, fewer than a thousand billionaires got $2.2 _trillion_ richer.

**That is the direct result of a rigged system that privileges the ultra wealthy while working people pick up the tab.**
Now, some of the wealthiest people in Washington state want even more.
A millionaire-funded ballot initiative, I-645, would repeal our new millionaires tax _before it even collects a single dollar_. That tax only touches income above $1 million a year — but repealing it hands millionaires and billionaires a whopping $13 billion tax break.
**This initiative is designed to take more money out of YOUR pocket and give it to greedy people at the top that just want another tax break.**
But Peter, the impact of I-645 will be even deeper than that. If it passes, it would slash critical state revenue, straining our hospitals and putting healthcare on the chopping block for tens of thousands of working people.
We don’t have to accept a system that prioritizes the 1% over the safety of working people. [**If you’re able, please pitch in $3 today to help me keep fighting back against billionaire greed and defeat this dangerous initiative.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261022.RYZRFU&refcode=em20261022-6869&amount=3&t=3&akid=6869%2E420207%2EYy7dor)

Pete Hegseth's proposed livestream of an execution may have been shut down after righteous backlash sounded from around the country. As a retired general, I can tell you that the military carries out its most difficult missions with dignity, respect, and a quiet discipline that honors those who serve. Pete Hegseth thinks it's okay to turn it into a horrific reality TV show, and that's downright disgraceful--and it says more than he might realize about his ability to do his job. Take this _New York Times_ headline.

As the article goes on to say: **_" Men with real accomplishments on the battlefield don't tend to talk this way."_** After 40 years in uniform, I couldn't agree more. This job is simply too big for Pete Hegseth to handle. Discipline, judgment, and accountability are not optional in military leadership. Hegseth has shown none of them. His amateurism is endangering our troops and making America less safe. **He needs to be fired -- and Clay Fuller can't be trusted to do it.** Our troops deserve far better from their leader, and they deserve far better from the members of Congress who refuse to hold that leader accountable. It's time to send someone to Congress who will stand up for our troops even when it's not politically convenient -- someone who will demand more from leadership and take real action to make it happen. clean_body: | | Pete Hegseth's proposed livestream of an execution may have been shut down after righteous backlash sounded from around the country. As a retired general, I can tell you that the military carries out its most difficult missions with dignity, respect, and a quiet discipline that honors those who serve. Pete Hegseth thinks it's okay to turn it into a horrific reality TV show, and that's downright disgraceful--and it says more than he might realize about his ability to do his job. Take this New York Times headline. | As the article goes on to say: " Men with real accomplishments on the battlefield don't tend to talk this way." After 40 years in uniform, I couldn't agree more. This job is simply too big for Pete Hegseth to handle. Discipline, judgment, and accountability are not optional in military leadership. Hegseth has shown none of them. His amateurism is endangering our troops and making America less safe. He needs to be fired -- and Clay Fuller can't be trusted to do it. Our troops deserve far better from their leader, and they deserve far better from the members of Congress who refuse to hold that leader accountable. It's time to send someone to Congress who will stand up for our troops even when it's not politically convenient -- someone who will demand more from leadership and take real action to make it happen. ~~ ~~ Thank you, Ret. Brigadier General Shawn Harris | | ~~ "Facebook" ~ "X" \[BLUESKY\] "Bluesky" PAID FOR BY SHAWN FOR GEORGIA

There are moments in a campaign when waiting is the most expensive decision you can make. This is one of them. **This week, I authorized our campaign to begin placing a new major television ad, even though we haven't finished raising the money to cover the full buy.** I don't love taking that kind of financial risk. But after my opponent, billionaire Rick Jackson, reserved $87 million in television advertising, I knew sitting on the sidelines wasn't an option. **[Will you make a contribution today between my campaign and Jasmine Clark to help keep our new ad on the air and respond to Jackson's unprecedented spending?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141988909/655434648/-1951883517?refcode=261022-risk-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDA0Y2FmMi03OWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uOxzaAvgK5N5GgIaHuoyRG7CrGI8Y3tLbvYSN82DxEg=)**

Rick Jackson is betting that if he spends enough money, he can hide the fact that he got rich by profiting off our health care. He wants to hide the fact that he promised to be “Trump’s favorite Governor,” and that there’s not a single thing he disagrees with Trump on. He's betting that an $87 million wall of television ads will drown out every volunteer, every organizer, every small-dollar donor, and every conversation about what's really at stake in this election. **I'm betting he's wrong.** But only if we have the resources to fight back. That's why I instructed my team to start locking in our own TV reservations. Every day we wait, ad inventory becomes more expensive, more limited, and more valuable. If we're going to compete, we have to claim our place on the air now—not months from now. It's a big commitment for a grassroots campaign. But this campaign has never been built on billionaire checks. It's been built by people giving what they can because they believe Georgia deserves a governor who will fight for working families—not another wealthy executive trying to buy public office. Rick Jackson may have $87 million reserved. We have each other. If thousands of people step up today, we can fund these ads, compete on the airwaves, and prove that Georgia's governor isn't for sale. **[Please make a contribution today to my campaign and Jasmine Clark to help fund our television campaign and defeat Rick Jackson this November.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141988911/655434650/-1951883517?refcode=261022-risk-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NjYwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDA0Y2FmMi03OWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uOxzaAvgK5N5GgIaHuoyRG7CrGI8Y3tLbvYSN82DxEg=)**

clean_body: | | | | = There are moments in a campaign when waiting is the most expensive decision you can make. This is one of them. This week, I authorized our campaign to begin placing a new major television ad, even though we haven't finished raising the money to cover the full buy. I don't love taking that kind of financial risk. But after my opponent, billionaire Rick Jackson, reserved $87 million in television advertising, I knew sitting on the sidelines wasn't an option. = = Rick Jackson is betting that if he spends enough money, he can hide the fact that he got rich by profiting off our health care. He wants to hide the fact that he promised to be “Trump’s favorite Governor,” and that there’s not a single thing he disagrees with Trump on. He's betting that an $87 million wall of television ads will drown out every volunteer, every organizer, every small-dollar donor, and every conversation about what's really at stake in this election. I'm betting he's wrong. But only if we have the resources to fight back. That's why I instructed my team to start locking in our own TV reservations. Every day we wait, ad inventory becomes more expensive, more limited, and more valuable. If we're going to compete, we have to claim our place on the air now—not months from now. It's a big commitment for a grassroots campaign. But this campaign has never been built on billionaire checks. It's been built by people giving what they can because they believe Georgia deserves a governor who will fight for working families—not another wealthy executive trying to buy public office. Rick Jackson may have $87 million reserved. We have each other. If thousands of people step up today, we can fund these ads, compete on the airwaves, and prove that Georgia's governor isn't for sale. = Thank you, Keisha Lance Bottoms = | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jasmine Clark for Georgia Jasmine Clark for Georgia 4370 Lawrenceville Hwy #96 Lilburn, GA 30048 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Peter, When I think about the toughest times in my life, I’m thankful I’ve always had a support system to help me through. I’m the proud daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. I know what it’s like to grow up in a family where working hard is necessary to pay the bills. That wasn’t always easy. Then Congressman Maurice Hinchey nominated me for West Point. I was the first in my family to graduate from college—that wasn’t easy. I deployed overseas six times, serving in combat zones like Iraq and Afghanistan. I was awarded three Bronze Stars. That certainly wasn’t easy. And today, running for Congress, less than two weeks away from Election Day, with Mike Lawler and the entire Republican party spending millions of dollars on attacking me—this hasn’t been easy either. Growing up, I had my family. In the Army and Special Ops, I had my soldiers. And in this campaign, I have you. I couldn’t do this without you, Peter. You probably didn’t wake up this morning thinking you were going to make a donation to my campaign, but I really need you to if we’re going to defeat Lawler and flip NY-17. Peter,

I don't say this to scare you. I say it because it's true.

This election is socialism versus freedom. Full stop.

The barbarians who hate this country are putting literal socialists into power right now. Zohran Mamdani. Abdul El-Sayed.

body:
Hi friend,

It’s hard to believe that more than a year and a half ago, I announced my campaign for Governor of New Mexico. What started as a promise to fight for our families, our communities, and our future has grown into a grassroots movement powered by people like you.

**And now, we’re just 12 days away from Election Day.
**
We’ve come so far together, but we still have so much to fight for. I’m running to build a New Mexico where every family can thrive, every child has the opportunity to succeed, and every community has a Governor who shows up and fights for them. **I’m giving this final stretch everything I’ve got, but I can’t cross the finish line without you.[_Will you rush $5 or more today to help us win this race and build a brighter future for every New Mexican?_](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1596-fr-nd&t=1&akid=13395%2E400544%2EWBom0E)**
---

---
With gratitude,
Deb
\---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: **Deb Haaland**
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025
Subject: Today, I’m launching my campaign for Governor of the great state of New Mexico.

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=3&akid=13395%2E400544%2EWBom0E)
---
I have exciting news, friend:

Today, I’m launching my campaign for Governor of the great state of New Mexico — my home — to bring our state together and build a bright future for all who live here.

I’m humbly asking: **_[Will you join our campaign as a day-one donor by donating just $5 or more?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1596-fr-nd&t=4&akid=13395%2E400544%2EWBom0E)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1596-fr-nd&t=5&akid=13395%2E400544%2EWBom0E)
---
The amount you give doesn’t matter. What matters is building a campaign with the support of real people. That’s who I am, who I came from, and who I am running to serve.

I am here today because my roots in New Mexico run 35 generations deep. My people lived on this land then, just as we do now. The Pueblo people were the first farmers in the high deserts of New Mexico.

I am here because of my grandfather, who worked for decades as a diesel mechanic on the railroad. Somehow he also kept a field — picking worms off the corn as it grew, like the generations before him.
I am here because of my grandmother, a survivor and a caretaker who woke up every day before the sun. She was the one who gave me my true love of cooking New Mexican cuisine. (She wouldn’t let us in the kitchen while she cooked, but I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours.)

I am here because of my parents and their sacrifice. My mother, a Pueblo woman, served in the Navy. My father, a Marine, received a Silver Star for his service in Vietnam. He now lies in honor at Arlington.

I am here because of my beloved child, who I raised on my own. I started a company to pay the bills, but it still wasn’t always enough. We relied on food stamps to get on our feet. I sometimes had to decide between paying rent and buying groceries to feed our family. I will never forget how that felt or the kindness of those who helped us — strangers who became community. When I look at my Somah, I see perseverance, strength, and hope.
These are my stories.

These are stories of New Mexico.

These days, our differences are blown so far out of proportion. We lose sight of a simple fact: We all live in the same state, together. All of us in New Mexico come from love, survival, and sacrifice. We all want to live good lives — and we want even more for our children.

Our President and his billionaire allies look at the lands and the people of this country and think: What can I exploit?
I am running to ask: If we come together in New Mexico, what good can we do for each other and for the next generation?

We have our work cut out for us. The cost of living is crushing our families. Our economy is growing, but we need to keep it going and make sure _everyone_ shares in our progress. Our farmers need more. Our families need more. New Mexico’s kids need so much more. And we must be good stewards of the Earth and preserve the rivers, mesas, farmlands, and forests whose beauty sustains our communities.
I am running to do all this and more. I am running to serve all New Mexicans and make sure we’re leaving a better future for our children.

**_[Will you join us with a day one donation?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17370?refcode=jtk1596-fr-nd&t=6&akid=13395%2E400544%2EWBom0E)_** I would be honored to have your support.
Be fierce,

Deb

The Pueblo people were the first farmers in the high deserts of New Mexico. I am here because of my grandfather, who worked for decades as a diesel mechanic on the railroad. Somehow he also kept a field — picking worms off the corn as it grew, like the generations before him. I am here because of my grandmother, a survivor and a caretaker who woke up every day before the sun. She was the one who gave me my true love of cooking New Mexican cuisine. (She wouldn’t let us in the kitchen while she cooked, but I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours.) I am here because of my parents and their sacrifice. My mother, a Pueblo woman, served in the Navy. My father, a Marine, received a Silver Star for his service in Vietnam. He now lies in honor at Arlington. I am here because of my beloved child, who I raised on my own. I started a company to pay the bills, but it still wasn’t always enough. We relied on food stamps to get on our feet. I sometimes had to decide between paying rent and buying groceries to feed our family. I will never forget how that felt or the kindness of those who helped us — strangers who became community. When I look at my Somah, I see perseverance, strength, and hope. These are my stories. These are stories of New Mexico. These days, our differences are blown so far out of proportion. We lose sight of a simple fact: We all live in the same state, together. All of us in New Mexico come from love, survival, and sacrifice. We all want to live good lives — and we want even more for our children. Our President and his billionaire allies look at the lands and the people of this country and think: What can I exploit? I am running to ask: If we come together in New Mexico, what good can we do for each other and for the next generation? We have our work cut out for us. The cost of living is crushing our families. Our economy is growing, but we need to keep it going and make sure everyone shares in our progress. Our farmers need more. Our families need more. New Mexico’s kids need so much more. And we must be good stewards of the Earth and preserve the rivers, mesas, farmlands, and forests whose beauty sustains our communities. I am running to do all this and more. I am running to serve all New Mexicans and make sure we’re leaving a better future for our children. I would be honored to have your support. Be fierce, Deb | | | | | |

I loved practicing medicine. I loved getting to know my patients and their families, watching children grow up, and being someone parents could turn to when they needed help.

But I also saw firsthand how difficult things could be for families who were doing everything right but still struggling to afford groceries, medicines, and the care they needed. **Their experiences are a big part of why I decided to run for Congress in the first place.**

---
Friends, last week I was on the Crooked Media podcast Hysteria to talk about something I think about a lot: our reproductive health data, who has access to it, and what can happen to it.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141989912/655459166/-642992695?amount=25&refcode=261022em_sjj_hysteria&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMzU5MWQ3OC04N2NlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=joBN8AZrp3Z-qnGSYkSICxGBTOt6Qe0SGW6FdV9NFwI=)
---
I want to share some of what I said because we should all be concerned about our data privacy, and about it falling into the wrong hands. **Right now, if you use a period tracking or fertility tracking app, your data is not protected by HIPAA.** And since Roe was overturned, your reproductive and sexual health data can be _sold to police_ and used to prosecute you in states where abortion is criminalized. It’s truly terrifying, and it’s already happening in red states. In Texas, a police officer accessed over 80,000 Flock cameras to track down a woman he was attempting to prosecute for seeking an abortion. In Nebraska, private Facebook messages between a mother and daughter were used as evidence against them during their prosecution for an abortion that was illegal under their state law. And data brokers have collected the information of people who visited hundreds of abortion clinics, packaged it, and sold it to anti-abortion groups who used it to target them with anti-abortion propaganda. _Here's what also concerns me: right now, a rogue agency or private company could theoretically use commercially available data to build a database of everyone's periods – and when someone misses a period, use that data to prosecute them for an abortion that's illegal in their state._ **This is part of Republicans' plans: Project 2025 explicitly called for a pregnancy surveillance system, and Trump's CDC director said that abortion surveillance is a “really critical component” of the agency's work.** Republicans will go to extraordinary lengths to control women's bodies, despite not having any actual understanding of women’s bodies. The federal government should have a role in protecting our most private and sensitive data. That's why I have introduced the _My Body, My Data Act_ multiple times — to create real federal protections and stop reproductive health data from being used to investigate, prosecute, or target people. **[Mike Johnson refuses to bring my bill to the floor for a vote, but this January, all of that can change if we win back the majority. clean_body: | | | | = Friends, last week I was on the Crooked Media podcast Hysteria to talk about something I think about a lot: our reproductive health data, who has access to it, and what can happen to it. = I want to share some of what I said because we should all be concerned about our data privacy, and about it falling into the wrong hands. Right now, if you use a period tracking or fertility tracking app, your data is not protected by HIPAA. And since Roe was overturned, your reproductive and sexual health data can be sold to police and used to prosecute you in states where abortion is criminalized. It’s truly terrifying, and it’s already happening in red states. In Texas, a police officer accessed over 80,000 Flock cameras to track down a woman he was attempting to prosecute for seeking an abortion. In Nebraska, private Facebook messages between a mother and daughter were used as evidence against them during their prosecution for an abortion that was illegal under their state law. And data brokers have collected the information of people who visited hundreds of abortion clinics, packaged it, and sold it to anti-abortion groups who used it to target them with anti-abortion propaganda. Here's what also concerns me: right now, a rogue agency or private company could theoretically use commercially available data to build a database of everyone's periods – and when someone misses a period, use that data to prosecute them for an abortion that's illegal in their state. This is part of Republicans' plans: Project 2025 explicitly called for a pregnancy surveillance system, and Trump's CDC director said that abortion surveillance is a “really critical component” of the agency's work. Republicans will go to extraordinary lengths to control women's bodies, despite not having any actual understanding of women’s bodies. The federal government should have a role in protecting our most private and sensitive data. That's why I have introduced the My Body, My Data Act multiple times — to create real federal protections and stop reproductive health data from being used to investigate, prosecute, or target people. = If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thanks so much for reading. — Sara = | | | Congresswoman Sara JacobsCalifornia’s 51st District = | = Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States | | | | | | ---|---|--- We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. | | | | Derek, I wanted you to hear from me after last night's debate. Like I said last night: _**Who is your governor going to work for?**_ I told you the GOP would spin anything and everything they can about last night, and they have a huge amount of money in the bank to do it. I'm proud of my campaign and what I'm fighting for. But I've learned not to get ahead of myself in this race.
Here's the thing: early voting is already open across Wisconsin, and the 9% of voters who are still undecided are making up their minds right now.
We need to respond to Tom Tiffany's lies, and we need to do it fast.
Congressman Tom Tiffany has $34 million from 2 far-right billionaire families. I don't have that. I have you, and thousands of grassroots supporters across Wisconsin.

name: Chris Deluzio
subject: For something.
body:
[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1001&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]Chris Deluzio for PA

Good morning, Willis.

If you are anything like me, your inbox and cell phone are littered with
last-ditch fundraising requests for candidates and causes. And those are
important – no doubt. This is the most important midterm election in
generations and we all have a role to play in taking back the House and
Senate.

But my hope is that with these messages you can get to know a bit more
about me and my work – so that when I do ask you to donate, you're not
just giving because you're against something (Trump, Republicans... John
Fetterman's latest failures and dereliction of duty), but that you're
giving before you are for something.

Last week, I had a debate with my Republican opponent in my House race.
Which, as you may know, is the last Democratically held battleground House
seat in Pennsylvania.

I talked about who I am and my work to take on corporate power.

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/877?t=1002&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]'Chris DeLuzio on Twitter: 'At 17, I first raised my right hand and
swore an oath to the constitution. I was willing to risk my life in
uniform because I believed America was worth fighting for. And it still
is. So I am humbly asking for your vote. To keep fighting for all of us.
To keep fighting to restore the American dream.''

About the impact of Trump's war and tariffs.

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/878?t=1003&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]'Chris Deluzio on Twitter: 'The record is clear: Donald Trump has made
your life more expensive. His reckless tariffs and failed Iran War are
driving up costs for hardworking Pennsylvanians.''

And the distrust I have for tech executives who prioritize profits above
all else.

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/879?t=1004&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]Chris Deluzio on Twitter: 'I don’t trust the fate of humanity in the
hands of AI tech executives who have nothing but profits in mind.'

We live today in the richest country in the history of the world.

And in the richest country in the history of the world, if you are working
hard and playing by the rules that ought to translate to a pretty good
life. I'm talking about more than just affording your life – which should
be the floor of our ambition. I'm talking about:

A roof over your head, deciding where you want to live, the ability to
pursue your passions and maybe start a business, put your kids in sports
and activities, send them to a good school, for your family to see a
doctor when you need one, maybe take a vacation now and again and retire
with dignity.

That is what I am for.

So I thank you for your help in defending this last Democratically held
battleground House seat in Pennsylvania. And I thank you in advance for
being there with me in whatever comes next.

Don't give up the ship,

Chris Deluzio

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

☀️ Wait ... Before you click away! 🇺🇸

Chris Deluzio has won his elections in a competitive House district
because of the support of grassroots supporters talking to voters, sharing
information online, and donating what they can.

If everyone getting this email contributed just $20 to his re-election, he
would win this November with ease and put Democrats one step closer to
taking back the House.

Unfortunately, not everyone gives—so he's counting on people like you who
know the stakes in this election to chip-in what they can.

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-26-q4.4eyHU-&refcode=em261023&t=1005&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]If holding this House seat and sending a fighter for working class
people like Chris Deluzio back to Congress is worth $20, please make that
donation today.

If you've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution
instantly:

[ https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/70?c0=deluzio-em-26-q4.e4Cayf&refcode=em261023&t=1006&akid=152%2E42639%2ERvTxmM ]CONTRIBUTE $20

clean_body: I just need 2 minutes of your time| | | | | Patriot, it’s John James. We're just 12 days away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next Governor of Michigan. Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming election for Governor on November 3rd. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. name: Josh Shapiro
subject: November 4th
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA]
body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, I’ve been
thinking a lot about Election Day. But I’ve also been thinking about the
morning after it.

There are only two versions of November 4th. In one, I go back to work —
and the right-wing agenda remains far away from the Governor’s Office.

In the other version, our opponent is preparing to take that desk, and
every one of those dangerous right-wing bills suddenly has a future. Not
in theory. In January.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19832?t=1001&akid=723%2E245147%2EEbY1r8 ]Eleven days decide which morning we wake up to, and almost all of what
happens in those days costs money — the ads, the doors, the calls to
people who haven’t decided. So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in
$15 toward the
version of November 4th you’d rather live in?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19832?t=1002&akid=723%2E245147%2EEbY1r8 ]Donate →

I want to be concrete about what those eleven days hold,
Derek.

There are two more weekends of canvassing. There’s the last stretch of
television ads. There’s one more round of mail that has to be printed
before it can be delivered. And there’s Election Day itself — the poll
monitors, the hotline, the rides.

That’s the whole list. Nothing on it is optional, and nothing on it gets
cheaper by waiting until the day before to act.

I’m not going to pretend I know how this ends,
Derek. Anybody in Pennsylvania
who tells you they know how a statewide race ends is selling something.

But what I do know is that the difference between those two mornings isn’t
fate. It’s a few thousand conversations that either happen in the next
eleven days. Or don’t.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19832?t=1003&akid=723%2E245147%2EEbY1r8 ]So please,
Derek: Chip in
$15 today
and help us fund a few thousand more of those conversations — because one
version of November 4th is an ordinary Wednesday in Pennsylvania — and the
other one is the first day Donald Trump gets a Governor who will
rubber-stamp his chaos, corruption, and cruelty.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

Thanks,

Josh Shapiro

Friends and Neighbors,
I’m sharing community highlights, updates from the Property Tax Truth Tour, and voting information for November 3.
I always appreciate the opportunity to hear directly from the people, organizations, local officials, and
business leaders who make our community stronger. These conversations help me better understand the challenges people are facing and the issues that deserve attention in Tallahassee.
And right now, one date is especially important: Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.

ELECTION 2026

Your vote is your voice
On Tuesday, November 3, voters across Marion County will decide races from the U.S. Senate and Governor’s office all the way down to our County Commission, School Board, and local districts. You’ll also decide three statewide constitutional
amendments, including one that directly affects what you pay to keep your home.
Think about this: the races that shape your daily life the most often get the fewest votes. Turnout drops the further down the ballot you go. But the people who set your property tax rates, run your schools, and decide how your roads get built are on that ballot too. If you skip them, someone else decides for you.

So here’s my ask. Make a plan to vote, and then bring someone with you.
VOTE BY MAIL
The deadline to request a mailed ballot was Thursday, October 22, at 5 p.m. If you already have a ballot, sign and
return it so the elections office receives it by 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3.
EARLY VOTING
October 22–31, 8 a.m.–6 p.m., at any designated early-voting location in Marion County.
ELECTION DAY

Tuesday, November 3. Polls are open 7 a.m.–7 p.m. local time. Vote at your assigned precinct.
BEFORE YOU GO
Bring current, valid photo identification with a signature. Check your registration, sample ballot, and voting location at VoteMarion.gov, or call 352-620-3290.
CHECK VOTING DETAILS →

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=hm7FF5CczM5liyD&b=uuTtrEjI6orSJG66wRF7PQ
Our freedoms were never meant to be a spectator sport. Read your sample ballot before you go, and don’t leave anything blank because it seems small.

LOCAL / MARION COUNTY

Around the district
Here are a few highlights from community events and conversations around the district. Photos reflect different occasions and are not all from October.

Give4Marion
There was plenty to celebrate as Give4Marion brought in more than $2.3 million for local nonprofits, with many exceeding their goals. Thank you to everyone who gave back to our community!

Supporting veterans
Conversations with VHV continued about the challenges facing local veterans and their families. Supporting those who served remains a priority for our office.

VOCAL
It was a pleasure to connect with VOCAL Co-Founder Linda Norman about the organization’s work in our community. We look forward to exploring ways to support their efforts!

Ocala Main Street
A conversation with Executive Director Sara Lambert offered a closer look at Ocala Main Street’s work and upcoming projects. Excited to explore how our office can support their efforts in downtown Ocala!

Firefighters and first responders
Proud to support Central Florida’s firefighters and first responders. Thank you to those who work every day to keep our communities safe!

A new home for a veteran family
Grateful for Habitat for Humanity of Marion County’s work with Army veteran Doug Haynes and his family through its Veteran Build program. Thank you to everyone supporting veterans and their families in our community!

SECO Energy
SECO Energy’s groundbreaking marked an exciting step toward a new operations center serving our growing communities. Proud to celebrate this investment in the reliable power our families and businesses depend on!

The Pearl Project
The Pearl Project helps families impacted by trauma through education, support groups, and resources like the Kid-2-Kid Foster Closet. Grateful for their work and proud to support their continued growth in Marion County!

Kids Central’s CARE Awards
Kids Central’s CARE Awards celebrated the dedicated staff and community partners who support children and families. Grateful for their commitment to making a difference in our community!

What I hear over and over is the same thing: people are working hard and still falling behind. The cost of living, insurance, and the cost of simply owning a home keep climbing. That’s not a talking point. It’s what families are telling me at kitchen tables across this district.

STATE / FLORIDA

The Property Tax Truth Tour

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=hm7FF5CczM5liyD&b=umsrglWDWJwVrxw2ighKMw

The Property Tax Truth Tour has continued across Central Florida, giving me an opportunity to speak directly with residents, elected officials, Realtors, community organizations, and local Republican groups about property taxes and the Amendment 3 proposal referenced throughout the tour.
Each stop has brought different questions and perspectives, and I appreciate everyone who has taken the time to participate in these conversations.

What’s on your ballot: Amendment 3
This November, voters will decide on Amendment 3, which came out of the Legislature’s special session this summer. Here’s what it does, in plain English:

• Raises the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, then adjusts for inflation.
• For people who had not maintained permanent Florida residence by December 31, 2026, the larger exemption begins in their fifth year of homestead exemption, to the extent permitted by the U.S. Constitution.
• Cuts the annual
assessment-increase cap for non-homestead property from 10% to 5% for non-school levies, beginning in 2027. This is an assessment cap, not a cap on the total tax bill.

• Restricts county and municipal property-tax spending to specified uses, including public safety, education, infrastructure, natural resources, debt service, retirement benefits, and administration. The text also allows other approved expenditures unless prohibited by general law.
It needs 60% of the votes cast on the amendment to pass. If approved, it would take effect January 1, 2027.
I see this as a real step, not the finish line.
My goal remains ending property taxes on the homes Floridians have already paid for, and I’ll keep fighting for that in Tallahassee.
Whatever you decide, read the amendment yourself before you vote. Don’t let anyone tell you what it says. Know it for yourself.

subject: Is this a conversation worth having?
disclaimer_text: paid for by megadonors who will never live a day under the result
body:
If I could have one more conversation with every Pennsylvanian before they vote, here’s what I’d say:

Derek, if I could have one more conversation with every Pennsylvanian before they vote, here’s what I’d say. This election isn’t about me. It’s about whether the person sitting in the Governor’s office answers to the good people of Pennsylvania or to Donald Trump and his far-right allies. That’s the whole thing. Every bill signed or vetoed, every budget, every decision about your schools and your freedoms runs through that one question. I’ve spent this entire campaign trying to have that conversation with the folks who haven’t had it yet. There are still a lot of them, and there’s still time to reach them. [**But the ones we don’t reach will decide the outcome of this race based on whatever they hear — and my opponent’s allies have a mountain of cash to make sure their version is heard first (even when it’s lies). So I’m asking directly: Will you chip in $10 to help us reach more of those voters before it’s too late?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141991382/655463087/-109723252?refcode=email_102326_closing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODA4ZTk2My1jYmNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1hRwdrvaEyMe8fqwi0JeLMmH663cPxXFYene6Re8JWk=) | | [Chip in →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141991383/655463088/-109723252?refcode=email_102326_closing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODA4ZTk2My1jYmNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1hRwdrvaEyMe8fqwi0JeLMmH663cPxXFYene6Re8JWk=)
---
Here’s who’s actually left to reach: Not the people who made up their minds in August.
It’s the Pennsylvanians working two jobs who haven’t followed most of our campaign, the ones who’ll decide in the car on the way to vote, the ones who’ve heard my opponent’s name exactly once. They’re still reachable, but only if we pay to be in front of them: A spot during the local news in Wilkes-Barre, a piece of mail in Bucks County, somebody at the door in Centre County on a Saturday morning.
And right now, those same people are hearing a very different version of me over and over — paid for by megadonors who will never live a day under the result.
Deadlines move money, and I’ll keep telling you when we’re up against one. But deadlines don’t move voters. What moves a voter is hearing something true at the moment they finally start paying attention — and that moment is right now.
[**So please, Derek: If that’s a conversation worth having, help us fund it by chipping in $25 today. Because Donald Trump has made it very clear what he wants from Pennsylvania — and the only thing in his way is a Governor who answers to you. Not him.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141991384/655463089/-109723252?refcode=email_102326_closing&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODA4ZTk2My1jYmNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1hRwdrvaEyMe8fqwi0JeLMmH663cPxXFYene6Re8JWk=)

clean_body: If I could have one more conversation with every Pennsylvanian before they vote, here’s what I’d say: Derek, if I could have one more conversation with every Pennsylvanian before they vote, here’s what I’d say. This election isn’t about me. It’s about whether the person sitting in the Governor’s office answers to the good people of Pennsylvania or to Donald Trump and his far-right allies. That’s the whole thing. Every bill signed or vetoed, every budget, every decision about your schools and your freedoms runs through that one question. I’ve spent this entire campaign trying to have that conversation with the folks who haven’t had it yet. There are still a lot of them, and there’s still time to reach them. = | | = Here’s who’s actually left to reach: Not the people who made up their minds in August. It’s the Pennsylvanians working two jobs who haven’t followed most of our campaign, the ones who’ll decide in the car on the way to vote, the ones who’ve heard my opponent’s name exactly once. They’re still reachable, but only if we pay to be in front of them: A spot during the local news in Wilkes-Barre, a piece of mail in Bucks County, somebody at the door in Centre County on a Saturday morning. And right now, those same people are hearing a very different version of me over and over — paid for by megadonors who will never live a day under the result. Deadlines move money, and I’ll keep telling you when we’re up against one. But deadlines don’t move voters. We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

# “Someone who I can turn to when times get tough.”
_-Chase Fleahman_
---
| | **Through Reed and the Bistro I found community**
I've known Reed for over 20 years. I first met Reed when I crashed his party celebrating the opening of his restaurant The Wild Hare Bistro. I soon found myself working for Reed as a cook at the Bistro. Reed took me under his wing and ignited in me a passion for food and community service. Through Reed and the Bistro I found community in the small town of Bemidji that I had only moved to a year before. Reed exemplifies the idea of Minnesota nice. He is kind, trustworthy, outgoing, and a little bit of a dork in the best way possible.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **He has consistently been someone who I can turn to when times get tough**
He will always make time for friends, and is as supportive of a person as you could hope to meet. **His work in and around the community with the homeless is just an extension of who he is as a person.** Reed lives his life as an example to others of the effect that true kindness, and honesty can have on those around you. I've been following politics since 2000 and have never seen a candidate more qualified for the office they are running for than Reed Olson.
Sincerely, _Chase Fleahman_

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Eyes on the prize
body:
We can’t put up our feet and start acting like North Carolina’s a done deal.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1719&source=&t=1&akid=4822%2E124072%2EGese6S) | | | |
---
Peter,
**I have a critical update to share with you:** Recently, Nate Silver’s Silver Bulletin has shifted his prediction for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate race further in our direction.
A lot of folks will hear that and think it means that we can rest on our laurels for these last 11 days. That we can pat ourselves on the back and put up our feet, since a win is guaranteed.
Having won my fair share of tough statewide races, trust me: **That couldn’t be further from the truth.**
While it means our campaign clearly has what it takes to flip this seat, it also means that the GOP is growing increasingly desperate to defeat me. Far-right super PACs have spent millions to broadcast despicable lies about my record on the airwaves, and BOTH President Trump and JD Vance just came for another recent hurrah to rally the MAGA base in Greenville and Hendersonville.
The tides may be turning against Republicans in North Carolina and nationwide, but Senate control still hinges on the outcome of our race. **Your grassroots support toward our daily fundraising goal is the only way I’ll fight back against any surprises they still have up their sleeves and cross the finish line first on Election Day.**
[**_So if you care about flipping North Carolina blue and taking back the Senate as much as I do, will you chip in your first donation of $5 now to power our movement to victory?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1719&amount=5&t=8&akid=4822%2E124072%2EGese6S)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Six states. Two weeks.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
T minus 11 days to the election, let’s not slow down now

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3059%2E4032634%2EY7OrvS)
---
_10/10: Michigan for Dr. Abdul El-Sayed_
_10/17: Maine for Troy Jackson and Hannah Pingree_
_10/19: New Mexico for Deb Haaland_
_10/20: Nevada for Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and Attorney General Aaron Ford_
_10/23: Georgia for Senator Jon Ossoff_
_10/25: New Hampshire for Chris Pappas_ _And more soon!_ My campaign schedule for these final weeks before Election Day has been packed — and I’m feeling energized. Six states in just over two weeks, rallying voters for Democrats I’m proud to stand alongside. And I’m not slowing down. Today, I’m in Georgia campaigning for my friend Jon Ossoff. On Sunday, I’ll be in New Hampshire with Chris Pappas. I’m doing everything I can to help Democrats win up and down the ballot, because the stakes in this election couldn't be higher. This fight is about more than who holds the majority in Congress. It’s about whether anyone in Washington will stand up to Donald Trump. It's about whether we can lower costs for working families, protect people's rights, and stop billionaires and giant corporations from writing the rules for everyone else. Trump wants two more years with a Congress that rubber-stamps his agenda and lets him do whatever he wants. We cannot give him that kind of unchecked power. We need to hold his administration accountable. And we need to fight for an agenda that puts working people first: affordable child care for every family, a wealth tax so billionaires finally pay their fair share, a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, and real guardrails on AI so Big Tech can't put profits ahead of people. That's what's on the line in a few short weeks. And we have the power to make it happen. But winning these races takes more than good candidates and good ideas. It takes organizers knocking on doors, canvassers talking to voters, and grassroots supporters helping Democrats compete in communities across the country. That's why I'm reaching out to you today. [**This movement runs on grassroots supporters like you. Will you chip in $28 right now to help power the final push and elect Democrats up and down the ballot who will stand up to Trump?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3868?amount=28&t=8&akid=3059%2E4032634%2EY7OrvS)

# **Whatever November 3rd Brings, Thank You.**
**In just 11 days, we'll find out whether Texas has been listening.** Whichever way the pendulum swings, my message has never changed: public service is about people, not power. It's about showing up, listening, and fighting for communities that deserve to be heard.**As Election Day approaches, I want to take a moment to say thank you.** To everyone who has opened their doors, shared their stories, volunteered their time, offered words of encouragement, or simply believed in what we're building, I am deeply grateful._Four campaigns_ have given me the privilege of meeting extraordinary people across Texas. You've reminded me that the strength of our communities lies not in Washington, but in the people who call them home.Regardless of the outcome, I am proud of the conversations we've started, the relationships we've built, and the voices we've brought into the conversation.**Before Election Day, here are a few important dates to remember:** October 30: Last day of early voting in Texas; November 3: Election Day. Visit [_VoteTexas.gov_](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/EAAACZ1NIn4AAc7kw-AAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBq20yPt7SD_fAaSbyvfBcF7w8StgAtq28/2/yv-1r6w_ME8WIyAO18mH-w/aHR0cHM6Ly9Wb3RlVGV4YXMuZ292) for official voting information and polling locations.**And if you don't live in District 8, please share this message with someone who does. Every conversation matters.**

I want to start with two words: **Thank you.**

But this race is far from over. We're facing an unprecedented wave of outside spending from the other side, and what we do in these final two weeks will decide this seat. Every conversation, every door, and every vote count.
I recorded a short video for everyone who has helped get us this far. I'd appreciate it if you took a minute to watch it. I've also included what I said below.

Chris
