I wanted to take a minute to talk directly to everyone who's supporting this campaign to say: Thank you.
From the very beginning, this campaign has been about the people of New Hampshire, and it's been powered by folks who believe in what we're doing here.
Whether you chipped in what you can, volunteered your time, talked to your friends and neighbors, put up a yard sign, or found your own way to help, it all adds up.
And I don't take any of that for granted.
When you're in the middle of a campaign, there's always another deadline, another event, another conversation to be had.
But I always try to find the time to stop and thank the people who have helped get us to this point.
It means a lot to me.
We've built a great grassroots campaign together.
People all across New Hampshire and the country have stepped up, and they've made this campaign what it is.
I'm really proud of that, and I hope you are too.
So thanks for your support. Thanks for your trust. And thanks for everything that you're doing to get us to this point.
I'm really grateful to have you on the team, and let's finish this strong.
Let's show the rest of the country what we can do here in New Hampshire when we work together.
Thanks.

subject: Your dollar goes further here than anywhere

body:
Our best chance to unseat Tim Burchett

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/1074df929046/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363980?e=dc5f639d62)

|

| | | | |
---
|
---
| |

Friend,
I know what it takes to campaign in Tennessee. Grit. Determination. Hope, amidst a chorus of naysayers who think that Tennessee is too red to flip. An unwavering belief that our community is worth fighting for.
I know that none of that comes as a surprise to you.
**But what might surprise you is how much further your dollar goes here in Tennessee.** It’s true.
Our media markets are smaller and ad buys are cheaper. Overconfident Republican incumbents (like Rep. Tim Burchett) don’t think they have to work that hard to defend their seats.
They don’t know how to run a modern campaign and earn votes because they don’t think they have to – so every mailer, postcard, and text sent, every door knocked, and every ad has a better chance of actually reaching a persuadable voter.
All of this means that every dollar goes further in Tennessee.
My friend, Michaela Barnett, has been running a phenomenal campaign to unseat Tim Burchett.
I’m so proud of what she and her team of supporters (me included!) have built over the past year plus: 1300 volunteers. 21 people on payroll. Thousands of doors knocked every week. Over 12,000 postcards sent. Over 220,000 voters already contacted – and a week and a half to ensure that every single supportive voter gets to the polls.

To keep running as hard as she has been this past year, Michaela needs to raise another $50k by election day. In another race, that would be a drop in the bucket of a multi-million dollar budget. **In this race, it makes all the difference.**
**Will you join me in chipping in to ensure Michaela has the resources she needs to beat Tim?**
[**CLICK HERE TO DONATE!**](https://us.list-manage.com/kdr2a3qesMz?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)****

In Solidarity,
Rep. Gloria Johnson

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: The greatest trick the oligarchs have played
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
I get it.
#
One of the greatest tricks the oligarchs in this country have played is to convince the working class of this country that they have the money, they have the power, they'll buy all the candidates and elections they want and there is absolutely nothing you or your neighbors can do about it.
I get it.
I come from the Bronx.
And for so long, what was so hard about it was feeling like we were growing up in a place where no one cared about us. Where no one saw us, where our issues were not addressed, where our community wasn’t invested in. And for a very long time, a lot of us would just kind of throw up our hands and just say, well, no one’s really fighting for us.
But that feeling is not unique to the Bronx. It is happening all over this country.
A lot of times when people talk about the lack of voter engagement, they talk about it as though that’s the person’s problem.
But like any other relationship in life, the relationship between a government and its citizens is a two-way street.
And today we have a government that makes a lot of people feel like they don't matter. And so why would a person step up and participate in a situation where they are dismissed?
I am here to tell you if there was ever a time to shake off that understandable cynicism and to refuse to surrender to despair, that time is now.
Because if you look back throughout the history of this country and many others around the world, real change that benefits the working people almost never occurs from the top down. It only happens when regular folks shake off the cynicism and despair they feel and act to fight against injustice.
Will it be easy?
Of course not.
Will we be successful?
There is too much at stake not to try.
First: we do everything we can to win this election, flip the House and Senate and put a check on Donald Trump's power.
Then we must build upon that success and continue the organizing work we've done not just to win an election, but to fight for a government that works for all people and not just the oligarchs spending billions of dollars in this election.
Thank you for reading.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

* * *

**🇺🇸 Wait... before you click away ⛅️**
Alexandria is not running around the country begging billionaires for campaign contributions. Our work is funded by lots and lots of people making individual donations when they can, for whatever amount they can.
The donations we do receive go toward things like the organizers we've hired in Tennessee and Florida, toward events and travel when you see us holding things like the Fighting Oligarchy Tour, or time on the road supporting Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Emilia Sykes in her competitive House race in Ohio.
The donations we receive sometimes go toward donations we make to candidates like Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania before he won his primary -- and they go toward worthy causes like the Northeast Bronx Community Farmers Market Project or the Bronx River Houses Residents Association.
[Can you please make a contribution to support Alexandria's work today? Our average donation is around $16. Some give more. Some give less. There is a small piece of every donation made in all of the work our campaign does.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261023-12470-P_FND_EGR_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12470%2E2526796%2E2asWDD)

clean_body: Florida deserves better than this. | | | | | ---|--- Peter, Angie Nixon here. Republicans have controlled Florida for years, and they cannot hold that much power while pretending they bear no responsibility for what working families are experiencing: grocery bills that keep climbing, rent and insurance eating up paychecks, childcare families can't afford, and healthcare that costs too much. Here's what Republicans understand about me, and why it scares them. I just shocked the political establishment by winning the Democratic nomination despite being dramatically outspent, proving that people-powered organizing can beat big money. I'm a working-class Black woman who isn't going to Washington to protect wealthy donors or preserve the status quo. I've been clear about why I'm running: I want government to work for working people instead of the wealthy and powerful interests that have dominated Washington and Tallahassee. The wealthy and powerful keep getting richer while working people are told to make do with less. Early Vote Action

Peter, Let me explain why I'm so fired up about ballot chasing -- because the math is beautiful. Every Republican vote we "bank" early frees campaigns to stop chasing that voter and focus everything on turning out the people who haven't voted yet. Bank 20,000 votes early, and the path to victory gets dramatically easier. And study after study shows there's nothing more effective than a knock on the door. That's what my team does -- using daily data to find who has a ballot and sending activists to make sure it gets returned. Chasing ballots = banking votes. The more chasers you help fund, the more races we win.

A note from Senator Ashley Moody |

Friend,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: One Fight
body:
We’ve come so far. Let’s go win this.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Last week, we officially kicked off our One Fight Tour. We’ve been traveling across Texas to meet with voters, talk about what’s at stake in this election, and make sure Texans are ready to cast their ballots.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=1&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8) | [](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=2&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)
---|---
Since launching this campaign, I’ve traveled thousands of miles across our great state, meeting thousands of Texans who feel like they’ve been left behind by Greg Abbott. I’ve heard the same thing over and over again: **Texans are working harder than ever, but getting less in return.**
That’s why I’m running for Governor.
For too long, Greg Abbott has put the interests of his billionaire donors ahead of hardworking Texas families. Our neighborhood schools are struggling, everyday costs are soaring, and the American Dream is slipping further out of reach.
But everywhere I’ve traveled, I’ve met Texans who believe, just like I do, that it’s time for change.
And now, with multiple independent polls showing us ahead of Greg Abbott, we’re closer than ever to making that vision a reality.
We’re taking that momentum on the road with one message:**There’s only One Fight this November — will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires’ world and we just live here?**
I’m fighting to make sure we realize the vision of Texas where we all have a seat at the table and the rich and powerful don’t get to dictate how the rest of us live.
If you’re with me, help me keep this campaign on the road meeting Texans from now until Election Day. **[Support our fight with a $5 contribution now.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=3&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-2516&t=22&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)
We’ve come so far, but we are not done yet. With just weeks left until Election Day, every conversation, every door knocked, and every vote will make a difference.
Texans are ready for change, and this November, with your support, we’re going to make it happen.
Let’s go win this thing!
Gina

| | Peter, We want you to remember these five names, because what they're doing has NEVER happened in American history: **we have five Indigenous women on the ballot in one election, three of them running for top statewide offices.** **Mary Peltola** finished 8 points ahead of a sitting Republican senator in Alaska's primary in a state Trump won by 13. _NPR now calls her race the "majority maker" for the entire Senate._ **Peggy Flanagan** could join Peltola as the first Native American women EVER to serve in the U.S. Senate representing Minnesota. **Deb Haaland** would be the first Native woman ever elected governor, and she's the clear front-runner in New Mexico. And **Sharice Davids** and **Claire Valdez** are fighting to grow Indigenous representation in the House. All five are tied or ahead. Leading in September is nice. Winning in November is better. And this is the stretch when the ads get bought, the field programs scale up, and the other side's money arrives. clean_body: Remember these names Remember these names | ~~ | | Peter, We want you to remember these five names, because what they're doing has NEVER happened in American history: we have five Indigenous women on the ballot in one election, three of them running for top statewide offices. Mary Peltola finished 8 points ahead of a sitting Republican senator in Alaska's primary in a state Trump won by 13. NPR now calls her race the "majority maker" for the entire Senate. Peggy Flanagan could join Peltola as the first Native American women EVER to serve in the U.S. Senate representing Minnesota. Deb Haaland would be the first Native woman ever elected governor, and she's the clear front-runner in New Mexico. And Sharice Davids and Claire Valdez are fighting to grow Indigenous representation in the House. All five are tied or ahead. Leading in September is nice. Winning in November is better. And this is the stretch when the ads get bought, the field programs scale up, and the other side's money arrives. It's the most expensive eight weeks of these campaigns' lives, and it starts now. Indigenous Women Lead PAC exists to fight for each of these women between today and Election Day. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | - ~~ Let's make sure the history books remember all five of these women. name: Eric Pratt
subject: My Story and Vision for Minnesota
body:
Here is the lesson that guided my entire life.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/QM8_DuDZHk2?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

My family moved to Prior Lake back in the mid-1970s. My dad worked in real estate, and my mom spent 25 years teaching school right in Shakopee.Growing up here, you learned early on that people look out for their neighbors. It wasn't about titles or politics. It was about taking pride in an honest day's work and showing up when someone needed help.My parents taught me a simple lesson that stayed with me my entire life: **work hard, take responsibility, and when something is broken, you step up and fix it yourself.**
---
| [JOIN MY TEAM & HELP US WIN MN-02 >>](https://us.list-manage.com/bg4CJv9fOnr?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

That exact mindset carried me onto the football field at the University of Colorado under Coach Bill McCartney, through my MBA, and across 30 years in banking and financial risk management. In business, if you ignore problems or mismanage a balance sheet, you fail. You have to prevent fraud before it happens, protect every dollar, and deliver real results.When I served on our local Prior Lake–Savage School Board, we brought those same common sense principles to government: eliminating debt, building a budget surplus, and lowering property taxes while making our schools better for our kids.Now, families across our district are getting squeezed by sky-high prices at the grocery store and the gas pump. Meanwhile, out-of-state special interest groups are pouring dark money into MN-02 to protect their far-left agenda in Washington.My campaign is built entirely on grassroots support from neighbors like you across Dakota, Scott, Rice, Washington, and Le Sueur counties.When I get to Washington, I will fight to restore economic stability, stop government waste before it starts, and make sure our police have the backing they need to keep our neighborhoods safe. **But I can't do it without you taking the field with me.**
---

If you're ready for common sense leadership that actually delivers, I humbly ask for your support today.Thank you,Eric PrattCandidate for U.S. Congress (MN-02)

name: Newt Gingrich
subject: I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics. This is the fourth.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the NRSC
body:
I have been a first-hand witness to three disruptive moments in American politics. What I am watching build right now may be the fourth — and unlike the others, this one could go either way. | Peter,

I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics.

The first was Ronald Reagan in the late seventies and early eighties. People thought he was a cowboy who did not know what he was doing. Nine years later, the Soviet Union disappeared. That was a disruption.

The second was 1994, when I helped lead Republicans to the first House majority in forty years. We had a Contract with America. We had candidates who signed it. We had a grassroots base that understood exactly what was at stake. And we won because we did the organizing work before the election, not after it.

The third is Donald Trump, a disruptor whose legacy, I have said publicly, may rival the most consequential presidents in American history if the 2026 midterms go well for Republicans.

**_[Peter, that last part is the one I need to talk to you about.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f493781b845c40428cb74d59be1cb979&_e=oixP7vKWJ-gNKXm9lu2SS6QtdxQNlATzw7hPw83DO3UtWicAu9N89d-Io0ZNgyF23hB_8LMnuWp04GXCzSZz4pJBba-dZeMlHjtADPV1xCsbam7_n6-XRy2ot4QPKQp0AQIEirHFAtbAAPkTOj3pCP_dNcNdASur4fkzZnM9zJpXoMjLX-jODp2Sbd7YCS9NKjWJdw3CV6EBZ71-PpwiRkxmFGaVS98my9ehPmN0QIKTgRIn5ADVPxBK_ilUuXN2wByYolvn0B-y3bJPxhrupEopFeTHznOuLkDmemvCCHEpTTV5g_LoT9nq7EetoofakARxmmT1_ovQ1-rziI5qkZQTDfdK5D9GuKdeA7eASkYWY4H4ltQLVd0nzv7HFT7-lVkonRc9cmirsjHlcup_fst4Dkzp5_PAveO-XIO36MO6wsqzPYqvRtDqn6wIn80rh0a2mt_h8aH_uiYFfhbjrfEEE2j9JtXrCWzHO9nN2Fe0C2DkkzSDQKlDwPwbkdFdkOTbGFqJ3vHUQk8-tAHYs2vBCwwwaRKVxKWGLoZ8JtIZIwY1P0oo8YJR7ITmyjyWVUXsBEaWgIOFOIGGiTBybWHUSh7wEzqz8CZWSYJgkIfShlg30YjCg6QFl6L0QEchnIAJhU5_otlaQ3IaQV8I2ElxCp0aRQmy7AkQXqjfXmIIu9Bn5Zqm5Qgz3dTrq0NbVYucCRZX_BzsxdQfKRYrQHTzKeazlrJAVe2QiwZ7yg6QOq6XqyHHF549G_Cw2V1dBq3CfaT-sg8_jJGuliRSZRys1Mp9rpHcBTKbFawl11zgeMVs_CEQMtbSlK6slvjKA_HAqy51QeXmc9-RJ7zuKqUE33r_wC4RN2LExyFRP8yP2sy3x22eqVouCIJBEwSWdxZFXr8ZRtUGSDtDXrU8hwH3E9456H6cWpM0zQw7p_vutLGCW1kcsiwP-O9xbwoMTxKFYokOKTMXC7u1529Onm-Ux_lJ6YJkgiRXLIlmiHZ_HfBZCI7mx3YDhpSMcK6kSZdHZLdJ49kNqZv4o3DFOa5Mrhx82xPWoBJ6R5PF79ciJdhQZmE4uf6gwn0ACIFtrBtnahCXzmjyXX6MrNmQaQ%3D%3D)_ **

Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. When a mother sees her baby on the ultrasound screen and hears that tiny heartbeat, she has the opportunity to recognize the precious new life growing within her. **Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound and shares the hope of the gospel with a mother considering abortion.** And as our thank-you for your gift of any amount, we'll send you PreBorn!'s beautiful new **2027**** _Celebrate the Beauty of New Life_****Calendar!**

My daughter brought the washed greens to the table. I poured the pico de gallo over them, and as she began to mix--a jarring shift. From the television, the music in a political ad surged; ominous dread gave way to triumphant relief as the hero appeared. The music was not merely accompanying the images or words; it was manufacturing the hero.
Beethoven can carry us on an emotional journey through music alone, leaving our imaginations to supply the story. Joined to words and images, music can steer our judgment before we examine the evidence.
Emotion itself is not deception. But when music helps construct a story designed to guide our judgment, we must ask ourselves: Are we responding to the evidence, or to the feelings arranged around it?
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper. **
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

---
**Every single voter deserves 100% confidence that their vote is recorded accurately and counted as intended.** Early voting is in full swing across all 95 counties in Tennessee, and tens of thousands of Tennesseans are heading to the polls every day to make their voices heard. As voters cast their ballots, our TNDP Voter Protection team has received reports from voters who encountered issues at the voting machine. Whether you are voting early or planning to vote on Election Day (November 3rd), **please save these FIVE essential steps** so you know exactly what to do if you encounter an issue at your polling place: **📋 YOUR BALLOT PROTECTION CHECKLIST**
1. **FINISH YOUR BALLOT! Triple-Check Your Screen Selections:** Take your time at the voting machine. Before hitting "Print" or "Next," review the summary screen carefully to ensure every candidate highlighted matches your intended choice.
2. **Verify Your Printed Paper Ballot:** Tennessee voting machines generate a printed paper ballot summary. **Before feeding your paper ballot into the scanner, stop and read it.** Confirm that every candidate printed on the paper matches the choices you made on screen.
3. **Speak Up IMMEDIATELY If Something Is Wrong:** If the machine will not let you select your candidate, or if your printed paper ballot shows a discrepancy, **do NOT scan or submit the ballot.** Notify a poll worker immediately, explain the issue, and request assistance or a replacement ballot.
4. **Document the Details: **If you experience an issue or machine error, take note of your precinct location, the voting machine number, the time, and other relevant details.
5. **Call Our TNDP Voter Protection Hotline: 833-DEM-VOTE:** If you encounter any problem, are turned away without a clear reason, or witness improper voter intimidation, **call our TNDP Voter Protection Hotline immediately at 833-DEM-VOTE (833-336-8683).** Our dedicated team of trained volunteers and legal experts is on standby statewide to follow up, document reports, and connect you with immediate legal support.

If you ever have questions about your polling location or sample ballot, visit [**IWillVote.com**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142018633/655521523/327637188?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZDQxYmI0OS1lYWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sxNPP3U-2X6UulIVHzzbQ5tGT137hXL_PccXINSjzHY=&emci=fa7d4798-5ace-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=0d41bb49-eace-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=6362892) or call **833-DEM-VOTE.** Thank you for standing up for your community and exercising your fundamental right to vote. **Clay Capp**

name: Andy Matthews
subject: “Is it too late?”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ANDY FOR NEVADA
body:
Here's what we're doing now... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5860043?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1Ar5pU2GfJR?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

Yesterday afternoon, I got a call from a campaign supporter who had a direct question for me:

_“Is it too late to make a contribution that will make a difference?”_

Given that we are just 11 days from Election Day, it’s a fair question. But the answer is emphatically NO.

Here’s where things stand: The data we’re seeing come in as to early- and mail-voter turnout suggests this race is going to be very close. It’s even showing Republicans a little behind where we need to be, meaning that get-out-the-vote efforts need to be as effective as possible down the stretch.

That’s what my campaign is focused on now, and I’m hoping you can help.

If you’re able to [make a contribution today](https://us.list-manage.com/i1RgoF2j2A8?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), my team and I will put it directly into our efforts to contact Republicans who have not yet voted and urge them to get out and cast their ballot.

Not only is it not too late to make a contribution ... in many ways, this is an ideal time to do so.

In a race as tight as this one is likely to be, every vote counts. That’s why we’re working hard down the stretch to make sure no one sits this election out. That goes for you as well ... and so if you haven’t yet voted, be sure to make a plan to do so. (If you need information on how to find an early-voting location near you, go [here](https://us.list-manage.com/LtYzlkH_qwt?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73).)

You’ve been so generous, my friend, and I’m so grateful for your support. I hope you’ll consider one more contribution to help us reach as many voters as possible and make sure they get to the polls!

[You can contribute today by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/S9CtAN_mcAF?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Thank you so much, and I’ll be back in touch again soon!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy
